L0: It is a session-level error pattern used to identify inappropriate influence of a just-completed successful task on the next unrelated task.
L1: It is a session-level error pattern used to identify inappropriate influence of a just-completed successful task on the next unrelated task. After a high-confidence or successful task, agents carry over and replay its search, action, and validation sequence on the immediately following unrelated task, even when the task states are incompatible.
L2: It is a session-level error pattern used to identify inappropriate influence of a just-completed successful task on the next unrelated task within the same session. It occurs when agents carry over and replay search, action, and validation sequences from a high-confidence or successful task on the immediately following unrelated task: billing-oriented searches and validation were replayed on access-control tasks, and credential-reset actions were repeated on unrelated systems after billing recovery before incident response. It is read as the percentage of subsequent tasks affected, such as 14% of access-control tasks; clearing prior-session traces reduced this to 3%, and resetting session history reduced the pattern by 79%. It correlates with prior trace length rather than prior answer correctness. Reducing redundant page openings left the rate nearly unchanged, so shortening traces alone does not eliminate it. Clearing or resetting history substantially, but not fully, reduces it, modestly increases tool setup time, and has little effect on ordinary same-domain task performance.
